explanation:

agreeing to pay the land revenue to the government. This
system helped to protect the peasants from exploitation by
the government officials and intermediaries. It also gave

explanation:

was the third Mughal emperor of India and ruled from
1556 to 1605. He is known for his policies of religious
tolerance, administrative reforms, and promotion of arts
and culture. Akbar sought to create a more inclusive and
centralized empire by implementing policies that aimed at
integrating various religious and cultural communities into
his administration.

hold high administrative positions, and encouraged interfaith
dialogue. These measures earned him the reputation of an
“enlightened despot” who ruled with benevolence and
open-mindedness, focusing on the welfare of his subjects
regardless of their religious backgrounds.

pay 400,000 gold hun compensation to the Mughals, and
become a vassal of the Mughal empire. Additionally,
Shivaji’s son Sambhaji was to serve the Mughals with 5,000
horsemen in the Deccan.
